# Sirach Chapter 41 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 41 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**41:1** O death — how bitter the very thought of you is to someone living at ease, to someone free from worry, successful in everything, still strong enough to enjoy a good meal!

**41:2** O death — how welcome your verdict is to someone in dire need, whose strength has given out, who is worn down with age and overwhelmed by every care, who is stubborn and has lost all hope!

**41:3** Do not dread death's decree. Remember those who came before you, and those who will come after. This is the Lord's sentence upon all living flesh.

**41:4** Why struggle against what the Most High has ordained? Whether ten years or a hundred or a thousand — no one in Hades is called to account for how long they lived.

**41:5** Sinners' children are contemptible children; they make their home wherever the godless gather.

**41:6** The inheritance of sinners' children will be destroyed; their descendants will carry their shame forever.

**41:7** Children curse an ungodly father, because they suffer reproach on his account.

**41:8** Woe to you, you godless ones, who have thrown away the law of the Most High!

**41:9** At your birth, you were born into a curse; at your death, cursing is all you inherit.

**41:10** Everything that comes from the earth goes back to the earth — so the godless go from curse to destruction.

**41:11** People mourn over a dead body, but the foul name of the wicked is wiped out completely.

**41:12** Guard your good name — it will serve you longer than any treasure trove of gold.

**41:13** A good life lasts only so many days, but a good reputation lasts forever.

**41:14** My children, live your instruction in peace. Hidden wisdom, concealed treasure — neither does anyone any good.

**41:15** Better someone who hides their foolishness than someone who hides their wisdom.

**41:16** So take proper shame in the things I am about to name — for not every situation calls for the same standard:

**41:17** Be ashamed before your father and mother of sexual sin; before a ruler or a powerful person, of lying;

**41:18** before a master or mistress, of wrongdoing; before a whole assembly, of lawless behavior;

**41:19** before a companion or friend, of injustice; and in the neighborhood where you live, of theft.

**41:20** Be ashamed before God's truth and covenant; ashamed of lounging at table on your elbow;

**41:21** of grabbing without giving, of staying silent when someone greets you;

**41:22** of ogling a prostitute, of ignoring a relative who passes by;

**41:23** of taking someone's share without giving it back; of leering at another man's wife;

**41:24** of making advances to his servant girl — keep away from her bed;

**41:25** of insulting words to friends; of mocking someone after you've helped them;

**41:26** of repeating what you've been told in confidence; of betraying secrets.

**41:27** Then you will show real modesty, and everyone will love you for it.
